cases.question:
Serviced Office Space Lease Agreement

Preamble

With the help and success of Almighty God, this agreement is entered into in the city of Riyadh between:

1. saudi telecom company (stc), a Saudi joint-stock company established under Saudi laws and

regulations, registered under Commercial Registration No. 1010150269 in Riyadh, headquartered in

Al-Mursalat District, P.O. Box 87912, Riyadh 11652, represented in the signing of this contract by

Abdulaziz bin Abdullah Al-Qutai in his capacity as Vice President of Group Services (hereinafter referred

to as “saudi telecom company” or the “First Party”). 2. Saudi Cloud Computing Company (sccc by stc), a

legal entity headquartered in Riyadh, registered under Commercial Registration No. [Insert Number],

address [Insert Address], represented in the signing of this contract by [Insert Name], in his capacity as

[Insert Position] (hereinafter referred to as the “Second Party”).

The First Party and the Second Party are referred to individually as a “Party” and collectively as the

“Parties.”

Whereas the Parties desire to organize their contractual relationship regarding the leasing of a serviced

office space by the First Party, which includes necessary maintenance, operation, utilities (water and

electricity), office equipment, and any other requirements the First Party deems necessary to enable the

Second Party to utilize the space detailed in Article Two, the Parties, being of full legal capacity, have

agreed as follows:

Article 1: Status of the Preamble

The above preamble is considered an integral part of this contract, complementary to its provisions, and

shall be read and interpreted herewith.

Article 2: Purpose and Site Description

The Parties agree that the purpose of this contract is the allocation of the following space for the

administrative and office use of the Second Party (“the Leased Space”): - Area: 2,550 sqm - Property

Location: Riyadh, Building 8A - District: Al-Mursalat - Street Name: Imam Saud bin Abdulaziz - City:

Riyadh - Deed Number: 60856746564

Article 3: Term and Renewal

The duration of this contract is five (5) Gregorian years, commencing from the date of signing the

handover minute (“Effective Date”). Each contractual year shall be calculated from the Effective Date.

This contract expires at the end of its term. Should the Parties wish to renew it for a similar or different

period, notice must be provided 90 days prior to the expiration of the contract. The other party has 30 days

to accept or reject the request; failure to respond is deemed a rejection. If both parties agree to renew, this

shall be done via a written renewal addendum signed by both Parties, subject to the same terms and

conditions of this contract unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Article 4: Termination

1. Expiration of Term: The contract terminates automatically upon the expiration of its specified term

unless the Parties agree in writing to renew it according to Article Three.

2. Early Termination: Either Party may terminate the contract prior to the end of its term in the following

cases:

o If the other Party commits a material breach of the contract terms and fails to remedy it within thirty (30)

days of receiving written notification.

o If the other Party suspends operations, becomes bankrupt, ceases to function as an operating entity, or

if a third party takes action indicating the other Party is unable to pay its debts as they fall due.

o If either Party is excused from performing any obligation under Article Eight (Force Majeure) for more

than ninety (90) consecutive days.

3. Termination without Cause: The First Party may terminate this contract at any time and without cause,

provided it gives the Second Party fifteen (15) days’ written notice.

4. Legal Effects of Termination:

o All rights and obligations arising from the contract shall cease, except those which by their nature

survive termination, specifically the maintenance of confidentiality of information shared between the

Parties.

o The Second Party remains obligated to pay all outstanding rental amounts due to the First Party.

o Upon termination, the First Party shall notify the Second Party in writing at least 90 days before the

specified date to evacuate the leased premises.

Article 5: Value and Payment Method

1. Pricing: The rental rate per square meter is 2,429 Saudi Riyals. The annual rental value is 6,193,950

Saudi Riyals, and the total contract value is 30,969,750 Saudi Riyals.

2. Payment Schedule: Rent shall be paid to the First Party in a single payment at the beginning of each

contractual year.

3. VAT: Value Added Tax (VAT) shall be added to the amounts due in accordance with the Saudi VAT law,

its executive regulations, royal decrees, and ministerial resolutions. The First Party shall provide an

approved invoice compliant with Saudi VAT and electronic invoicing requirements.

4. Inclusions: The rental value includes periodic maintenance, cleaning of the site, water and electricity

costs, security, safety, insurance, furniture, and office services.

Article 6: Obligations

First Party Obligations

1. Hand over the Leased Space to the Second Party and enable its utilization without hindrance until the

end of the contract term.

2. Provide security, necessary maintenance, operation, utilities (water and electricity), and office

equipment as deemed necessary for the Second Party’s utilization.

3. Maintain common facilities including shared restrooms, roofs, emergency exits, elevators, stairs,

corridors, and parking lots.

4. Bear all maintenance costs resulting from the utilization of the Leased Space, provided the Second

Party notifies the First Party of maintenance needs in a timely manner.

5. Issue a comprehensive cooperative insurance policy (compliant with Islamic Sharia) for the rental unit

and its contents (decor, goods, etc.) against all risks, including fire, water leakage, floods, theft, natural

disasters, wars, and riots.

Second Party Obligations

1. Pay the rental value as specified in Article Five.

2. Use the unit for its intended purpose with the care of an ordinary person and in accordance with the

laws, customs, and traditions of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, bearing all penalties imposed by competent

authorities or the First Party for breaches of this obligation.

3. Preserve common facilities and use them properly for their designated purposes.

4. Provide all necessary documents required by the First Party to carry out the activity specified in this

contract.

5. Notify the First Party of any matter requiring intervention, such as urgent repairs, discovered defects, or

damages.

6. Comply with the First Party’s policies as provided from time to time, and remain responsible for any

breach caused by employees or subcontractors.

7. Return the rental unit to the First Party upon expiration or termination as per Article Seven.

8. Refrain from disposing of the unit or granting rights to its use to any third party without the First Party’s

prior written consent.

9. Bear the costs of any additional modifications requested by the Second Party.

10. The Second Party is permitted to make internal modifications or improvements provided they do not

contradict the primary purpose of utilizing the space.

Article 7: Handover and Return of Property

1. The Second Party acknowledges receipt of the Leased Space and confirms there are no objections.

2. Upon expiration or termination, the First Party shall send a formal written letter to the Second Party’s

address specifying the evacuation date. Evacuation must occur within a maximum of six (6) months from

the date of the letter.

3. If the Second Party or its representative fails to attend the handover appointment, the First Party may

take legal measures, claim compensation for the delay, and reserve the right to open and reclaim the unit

unilaterally.

4. A joint handover report shall be signed by both Parties specifying the condition of the site and any

damages incurred.

Article 8: Force Majeure

1. If either Party (the “Affected Party”) is unable to perform its obligations due to a Force Majeure event, it

shall not be held liable for such failure provided it:

o Sends a written notice as soon as practicable detailing the event and the estimated duration of the

inability to perform.

o Takes immediate action to minimize the duration and impact of the event.

o Resumes performance as soon as the Force Majeure event ceases.

2. If the Force Majeure event continues for more than thirty (30) days from the date of notification, either

Party may terminate the contract via written notice.

3. The Affected Party bears no responsibility for rights not provided to the other party due to the Force

Majeure event.

Article 9: Liability and Indemnification

1. Each Party is liable for direct damages caused to the other party due to a breach of obligations,

provided that liability shall not exceed the total annual rental value paid for the year in which the claim

arose.

2. Neither Party shall be liable for indirect, consequential, or special damages, including loss of profit or

business interruption.

3. The limitation of liability in paragraph (1) does not apply to claims brought by third parties. In such

cases, the responsible Party shall indemnify the other Party for all damages, losses, or expenses

(including attorney fees) arising from the acts or negligence of that Party, its employees, or contractors.

Article 10: General Provisions

1. Confidentiality: Parties shall not disclose information derived from this contract to any third party

without prior written consent, except to managers, agents, consultants, and employees, or as required by

the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

2. Waiver: Failure or delay by either Party to exercise any right shall not be deemed a waiver of that right.

3. Assignment: The First Party may assign or transfer its rights and obligations to another party with

notice to the Second Party. The Second Party may not do so without the First Party’s written consent.

4. Coordination of Works: The First Party must obtain the Second Party’s approval for any works within

the Leased Space at least thirty (30) days prior to execution.

5. Authority: Both Parties guarantee that their signatories are duly authorized to execute and implement

this contract.

6. Binding Nature: This agreement is binding upon the Parties and their successors. No amendment,

deletion, or addition is valid unless made in writing and signed by both Parties.

7. Notices: All notices must be in writing (Arabic or English), signed, and delivered personally or via

courier to the addresses listed above.

8. Severability: If any provision is found to be illegal or unenforceable, it shall be severed without affecting

the validity of the remaining provisions.

9. Governing Law: This contract is governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and any dispute

shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the courts of Riyadh.

10. Calendar: All periods mentioned are based on the Gregorian calendar.

11. Entire Agreement: This contract constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes

all prior explicit or implicit agreements, written or oral.

12. Language: This contract is executed in two Arabic copies, each serving as an original.

 

Please provide assessment for the above contract in the light of IFRS accounting standards !
cases.expected_output: Under IFRS 16, assess identified premises and customer control: distinct space, substantive substitution rights, economic benefits and use decisions. Bundled services do not exclude a lease. Allocate lease and non-lease consideration using relative stand-alone prices unless the lessee elects, by asset class, to combine associated non-lease components. The lessor follows IFRS 15 allocation. Assess furniture and equipment as potential lease components; only promises transferring goods or services create components. A lessor-only termination option does not itself shorten the lease term; extensions require enforceable rights. Resolve conflicting notice and evacuation clauses before finalising enforceability. On availability, recognise the lessee's right-of-use asset and liability unless an exemption applies. Discount unpaid lease payments using the implicit rate if readily determinable, otherwise the incremental borrowing rate. A commencement prepayment belongs in the asset rather than the unpaid liability. Do not invent values without allocation, commencement and a supported discount rate. Determine lessor classification from risks and rewards; operating-lease income follows the term rather than advance cash receipts.
cases.actual_output:
## **Conclusion:**

- **The agreement appears to contain a lease of office space together with service elements**, rather than being solely a service contract. This conclusion depends on confirming that the 2,550 sqm is a specifically allocated, physically distinct space and that Saudi Cloud Computing Company ("sccc") controls its use.

- **A five-year lease term is the appropriate starting assessment.** The First Party's unilateral right to terminate on 15 days' notice does not, by itself, reduce the accounting lease term to 15 days. The Second Party does not have an equivalent termination-for-convenience right.

- **The annual SAR 6,193,950 bundled charge should not automatically be treated entirely as payment for the office-space lease.** Lease and non-lease components need to be identified and the consideration allocated, unless an applicable lessee practical expedient is used.

- **A reliable numerical right-of-use asset and lease liability cannot yet be determined.** Outstanding matters include the component allocation, discount rate, actual commencement date, and the legal effect of conflicting termination and evacuation provisions.

## **Introduction:**

- This assessment considers the agreement from the perspectives of both saudi telecom company ("stc"), as the First Party and apparent lessor, and sccc, as the Second Party and apparent lessee.

- The principal accounting issue is whether the arrangement conveys control over identified office space, notwithstanding the extensive maintenance, utilities, security, furniture, and office services included in the price.

- The assessment uses only the supplied contract and accounting material. The material provides substantive guidance on lease identification, component separation, lease term, an illustration of initial lessee measurement, and operating-lease accounting by a lessor. Some other topics appear only in contents lists or indexes; those entries are not sufficient to establish their detailed accounting requirements.

## **1. Does the agreement contain a lease?**

### **1.1 Identified office space**

- The agreement identifies:
  - A space of 2,550 sqm.
  - Building 8A in Al-Mursalat, Riyadh.
  - Imam Saud bin Abdulaziz Street.
  - Deed number 60856746564.

- These details support the existence of an identified asset. However, the contract does not include a floor plan, floor number, unit number, or boundaries for the particular 2,550 sqm.

- **The relevant distinction is whether sccc receives a particular physical space or merely an entitlement to office capacity somewhere within the building.**
  - A physically distinct portion of a building can be an identified asset.
  - An unspecified capacity portion generally is not an identified asset unless it represents substantially all the capacity of the relevant asset.

- The handover minute and any attached premises plan are therefore important evidence. If they specify the exact premises allocated to sccc, they would strengthen the lease conclusion.

### **1.2 Substitution rights**

- No express right allows stc to relocate sccc to alternative premises throughout the contractual period.

- A substantive substitution right would require both:
  - The practical ability to substitute alternative premises.
  - An economic benefit to stc from making the substitution.

- stc's rights to terminate the agreement, undertake maintenance, or enforce policies are not, in themselves, rights to substitute the office space.

- **On the wording supplied, there is no identified substantive substitution right that would prevent lease accounting.**

### **1.3 Economic benefits from use**

- The office space is allocated for sccc's administrative and office activities.

- The obligation to hand over the premises and enable their use without hindrance supports the view that sccc receives the benefits of occupying the allocated space.

- Restrictions on transferring occupancy rights to third parties do not necessarily prevent sccc from obtaining substantially all the economic benefits within the permitted scope of use.

- The conclusion nevertheless depends on confirming that stc cannot simultaneously allocate the same premises to other customers.

### **1.4 Right to direct use**

- The agreement provides indications that sccc controls the use of the premises:
  - The space is allocated to sccc's own administrative and office activities.
  - sccc is responsible for its employees and subcontractors.
  - Internal improvements are permitted within the agreed purpose.
  - stc must obtain sccc's approval before undertaking works inside the premises.

- stc's maintenance, cleaning, security, utility, and building-operation responsibilities do not automatically give it the right to direct how and for what purpose sccc uses the office space.

- Restrictions concerning lawful use, safety, preservation of common facilities, and compliance with building policies appear capable of being protective rights rather than rights that determine sccc's business use.

- However, the requirement to comply with policies issued "from time to time" needs particular attention. If those policies merely regulate safe and orderly occupancy, they would not ordinarily undermine the control assessment. If they allow stc to determine substantive decisions about the space's use, further analysis would be necessary.

- **Overall assessment:** The agreement appears to convey control of office space to sccc, subject to confirming the specific premises, exclusive occupancy, and actual decision-making rights.

## **2. Effect of the serviced-office arrangement**

- The contract includes substantial services, but their presence does not automatically make the arrangement wholly a service contract.

- The supplied material expressly supports identifying a lease where a customer obtains a right to use an asset, even when significant services are bundled with that right.

- Similarly, annual advance payment does not prevent the arrangement from containing a lease. A right-of-use asset can exist even when some or all lease payments have already been paid.

- **Accordingly, neither the description "serviced office" nor the inclusive pricing is sufficient grounds to account for the entire agreement solely as service expenditure.**

## **3. Identification and allocation of contract components**

### **3.1 Office-space component**

- The right to occupy and control the identified premises is the principal apparent lease component.

- The full annual charge is a bundled contractual amount. The agreement does not separately price the office-space right.

### **3.2 Service elements**

- The agreement includes services such as:
  - Periodic maintenance.
  - Cleaning.
  - Security.
  - Office services.
  - Utility provision.
  - Building operation.

- These promises need to be assessed to identify the non-lease components to be accounted for separately from the office-space lease.

- The descriptions of "operation," "office equipment," and "office services" are broad. Their actual scope matters when identifying components and establishing stand-alone prices.

### **3.3 Furniture, equipment, insurance, and common facilities**

- **Furniture and office equipment should not automatically be treated as services.** Depending on the specific items and rights conveyed, the arrangement could contain additional rights to use identified assets.

- Access to parking and other common facilities should not automatically be treated as separate leases. The contract does not specify whether particular parking spaces or other assets are exclusively allocated to sccc.

- Insurance should not automatically be assigned a separate service allocation merely because it is listed among the rental inclusions. The relevant assessment concerns the nature of the promise and any benefit transferred to sccc.

- The supplied excerpts do not provide all the detailed guidance needed to resolve each of these component questions conclusively.

### **3.4 Allocation by sccc**

- Unless an applicable practical expedient is used, sccc should allocate consideration between the lease component and the aggregate non-lease components using relative stand-alone prices.

- Observable pricing should be used where available, including:
  - Comparable office-space rentals without the bundled services.
  - Separate supplier prices for comparable maintenance and cleaning services.
  - Comparable security and office-service charges.
  - Relevant equipment-rental prices.

- Where observable stand-alone prices are unavailable, estimates should maximise the use of observable information.

- The allocation principle can be expressed as:

**Annual amount allocated to the office lease = SAR 6,193,950 × Office lease stand-alone price ÷ Aggregate stand-alone prices of all identified components**

- This expression assumes the assessment results in one office lease component and other separately identified components.

- **The agreed SAR 2,429 per sqm is not, by itself, evidence of the stand-alone office rental price**, because that rate expressly includes the bundled services and other benefits.

### **3.5 Practical expedient**

- The supplied material recognises an exception to separate accounting where the lessee applies the relevant practical expedient.

- However, the full conditions and application requirements for that expedient have not been supplied.

- It would therefore be inappropriate to assume that sccc has elected it or that the full annual charge should automatically be incorporated into a single lease component.

### **3.6 Allocation by stc**

- stc must allocate consideration using the applicable IFRS 15 allocation requirements.

- The supplied material establishes that requirement but does not reproduce the detailed allocation provisions.

- stc should therefore establish its allocation independently under those requirements rather than assuming that sccc's accounting allocation determines stc's result.

## **4. Lease term and termination provisions**

### **4.1 Stated contractual period**

- The stated duration is five Gregorian years beginning when the handover minute is signed.

- The agreement does not give sccc a general right to terminate for convenience during that period.

- The five-year period is therefore the starting point for assessing the accounting lease term.

### **4.2 stc's 15-day termination right**

- stc may terminate without cause on 15 days' written notice.

- **That unilateral lessor right does not automatically reduce the lease term to 15 days.**

- The supplied guidance explains that a lease ceases to be enforceable under the bilateral termination principle when both parties can terminate without the other's permission and with no more than an insignificant penalty.

- Here:
  - stc has a termination-for-convenience right.
  - sccc has no equivalent general right.
  - sccc's early termination rights depend on specified circumstances.

- Consequently, the agreement should not be treated as a freely cancellable 15-day arrangement merely because stc can terminate it.

- **On the supplied facts, a five-year accounting term is supportable**, subject to the legal meaning and enforceability of the complete agreement.

### **4.3 Conflicting evacuation provisions**

- The contract contains different provisions concerning termination and return:
  - Termination without cause requires 15 days' notice.
  - Article 4 requires at least 90 days' notice before the specified evacuation date.
  - Article 7 requires evacuation within a maximum of six months from the formal letter.

- These provisions do not establish a clear, single timeline for when the right to occupy ends.

- The accounting implications depend on resolving:
  - Whether termination becomes effective after 15 days while occupation continues.
  - Whether the 90-day requirement limits the practical effect of the termination clause.
  - Whether Article 7 provides an enforceable occupancy right or only a deadline for completing evacuation.
  - Whether rent remains payable during any post-termination occupation.
  - Whether unused annual advance rent is refundable.

- **A maximum evacuation period should not automatically be added to the lease term.** A deadline for leaving is not necessarily an additional enforceable right to use the premises.

### **4.4 Renewal**

- Renewal requires agreement by both parties and a signed written addendum.

- sccc cannot unilaterally enforce an extension.

- **The initial lease term should therefore not include an additional renewal period solely because sccc expects or intends to remain.**

- The 90-day renewal request period is a procedural deadline, not an enforceable extension right.

### **4.5 Breach and force majeure**

- Rights arising from material breach, insolvency, or force majeure are conditional rights, rather than an unrestricted sccc convenience break.

- They should not automatically be treated as shortening the initial term to the relevant notice or remedy period.

- The force majeure provisions are inconsistent:
  - Article 4 refers to more than 90 consecutive days.
  - Article 8 permits termination after more than 30 days from notification.

- That inconsistency affects the interpretation of the parties' rights if such an event occurs. It does not, by itself, demonstrate that the initial lease term is only 30 or 90 days.

## **5. Commencement date**

- Lease identification is assessed at contract inception.

- The lease term begins when stc makes the premises available for sccc's use.

- The contract links its Effective Date to signing the handover minute. That date is appropriate for accounting commencement if it also reflects actual availability of the premises.

- Evidence relevant to that assessment includes:
  - The signed handover minute.
  - Identification of the premises delivered.
  - Access arrangements.
  - Readiness of the space for its contracted use.
  - Any conditions preventing sccc from using it.

- Article 7 states that sccc acknowledges receipt, whereas Article 3 links commencement to a handover minute. These provisions should be reconciled with the actual delivery facts.

- **The signing date of the lease agreement should not automatically be substituted for the date the premises become available.**

## **6. Initial accounting by sccc**

### **6.1 Contractual amounts**

- The contractual arithmetic is consistent:
  - 2,550 sqm × SAR 2,429 = SAR 6,193,950 annually.
  - SAR 6,193,950 × 5 years = SAR 30,969,750.

- These are undiscounted bundled amounts before the separately added VAT.

- **SAR 30,969,750 is not automatically the initial lease liability**, because component allocation, advance payment, and discounting must first be addressed.

### **6.2 Annual payments in advance**

- The supplied initial-measurement illustration demonstrates that a payment made at commencement is included in the right-of-use asset, while the lease liability represents the present value of payments remaining unpaid.

- Applying that illustration to this contract, and assuming:
  - A five-year term.
  - Equal annual amounts allocated to the office lease.
  - The first annual lease payment is made at commencement.
  - Four further payments fall due at annual intervals.

- Let:
  - **L** represent the annual amount allocated to the office lease.
  - **r** represent the appropriate annual discount rate.

- The initial lease liability would be:

**Lease liability = L ÷ (1 + r) + L ÷ (1 + r)² + L ÷ (1 + r)³ + L ÷ (1 + r)⁴**

- Before any other supported adjustments, the initial right-of-use asset would be:

**Right-of-use asset = Initial lease liability + L**

- This formula is an illustration of the measurement mechanics, not a completed valuation. Different payment dates or payment status would require corresponding changes.

### **6.3 Discount rate**

- The supplied measurement illustration uses the lessee's incremental borrowing rate when the rate implicit in the lease cannot readily be determined.

- No appropriate rate is provided for sccc.

- A rate from one of the supplied illustrations should not be imported into this contract without supporting facts.

### **6.4 Other initial amounts**

- The supplied illustration also demonstrates adjustments for qualifying initial direct costs and lease incentives.

- No quantified initial direct costs or lease incentives are identified in this agreement.

- No additional amounts should therefore be inserted into the valuation without evidence.

### **6.5 Limits of the supplied measurement material**

- The supplied contents lists identify subsequent measurement, presentation, and disclosure topics, but do not reproduce their detailed requirements.

- Accordingly, the material supports the initial measurement approach above, but not a complete numerical subsequent-accounting assessment.

## **7. VAT**

- VAT is contractually added to the stated amounts, and stc must issue compliant invoices.

- The agreement does not specify the applicable VAT rate or establish sccc's recovery entitlement.

- Although the supplied contents lists identify VAT as an accounting topic, they do not provide the substantive guidance needed to determine its treatment in the lease liability and right-of-use asset.

- **No VAT-inclusive lease valuation can therefore be supported from the supplied material alone.**

## **8. Accounting considerations for stc**

### **8.1 Separation of lease and service consideration**

- stc should not treat the entire bundled payment as office rental income without assessing the components and allocating the consideration.

- Its lease-component accounting should be distinguished from the accounting for the services promised under the agreement.

- The supplied IFRS 15 material establishes the allocation requirement, but is insufficient for a complete service-revenue recognition analysis.

### **8.2 Conditional operating-lease treatment**

- If the office-space lease is accounted for by stc as an operating lease:
  - The underlying asset remains recognised according to its nature.
  - Depreciation or amortisation follows the normal policy for similar assets.
  - Impairment is assessed under the applicable impairment requirements.
  - Lease income is recognised over the lease term on a straight-line basis unless another systematic basis is more representative.

- **Receipt of an annual payment in advance does not, by itself, justify immediate recognition of the full year's lease income.**

- If the annual lease allocation is constant, that allocated amount would generally be recognised over the corresponding year, rather than wholly on the payment date.

- Any qualifying initial direct costs of arranging an operating lease are added to the underlying asset's carrying amount and expensed over the lease term on the same basis as lease income.

- These observations are conditional accounting consequences, not a definitive determination of the lessor's lease classification.

## **9. Matters preventing a fully quantified conclusion**

### **9.1 Premises and control evidence**

- The precise physical boundaries of the 2,550 sqm.

- Confirmation of exclusive occupancy and any relocation or substitution arrangements.

- The substance of stc's policies and whether sccc retains the relevant use decisions.

### **9.2 Commercial and valuation evidence**

- Stand-alone prices for the office-space right and other identified components.

- Identification of the furniture and equipment supplied.

- The actual commencement date and payment dates.

- The appropriate discount rate.

- Any qualifying initial direct costs or incentives.

### **9.3 Contract interpretation**

- The interaction between the 15-day termination notice, 90-day evacuation notice, and six-month evacuation deadline.

- The treatment of prepaid rent following early termination.

- Whether occupation after termination carries enforceable rights and payment obligations.

- The conflicting force majeure termination periods.

### **9.4 Overall assessment**

- **The most supportable conclusion is that this is a mixed lease-and-service arrangement with an initially supportable five-year lease term.** Neither the service bundle nor stc's unilateral 15-day termination right provides sufficient grounds to treat it automatically as a service-only contract or a 15-day lease. Final measurement depends on confirming the premises and control rights, allocating the bundled consideration, establishing commencement and the discount rate, and resolving the contractual inconsistencies.

**Exceptions, Waivers & Special Conditions:**
- **Practical Expedient:** sccc may elect, by class of underlying asset, to combine each lease component with its associated service components and account for them as a single lease component, increasing the lease liability and right-of-use asset compared with separate accounting. This election is unavailable to stc as lessor, which must still separate lease and non-lease components.

- **Special Condition:** Included furniture and office equipment constitute separate lease components only if sccc can benefit from each asset independently or with readily available resources, and the assets are neither highly dependent on nor highly interrelated with the other underlying assets. Otherwise, those rights of use form part of a combined lease component rather than automatically being treated as separate equipment leases.
